{{Infobox football match | title = 2020 Coupe de France final | image = StadeFranceNationsLeague2018.jpg | image_size = | caption = The [[Stade de France]] hosted the final | event = [[2019–20 Coupe de France]] | team1 = [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] | team1association = [[Ligue 1]] | team1score = 1 | team2 = [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] | team2association = [[Ligue 1]] | team2score = 0 | details = | date = {{Start date|2020|7|24|df=y}} | stadium = [[Stade de France]] | city = [[Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis|Saint-Denis]] | man_of_the_match1a = | referee = Amaury Delerue | attendance = 2,805{{refn|group=note|name=Behind closed doors2}} | weather = | previous = [[2019 Coupe de France final|2019]] | next = [[2021 Coupe de France final|2021]] }} The '''2020 Coupe de France final''' was a [[association football|football]] match between [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] and [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] to decide the winner of the [[2019–20 Coupe de France]], the 103rd season of the [[Coupe de France]]. The final was originally scheduled for 25 April, but was postponed to 24 July due to concerns over the [[COVID-19 pandemic in France]].{{cite web|url=https://www.stadefrance.com/en/ticket/finale-coupe-de-france-2020|title=2020 French Cup Final|website=stadefrance.com|publisher=Stade De France|access-date=4 March 2020|archive-date=26 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726163537/https://www.stadefrance.com/en/ticket/finale-coupe-de-france-2020|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/ro106148/md0/results-and-standings/|title=France » Coupe de France 2019/2020 » Final|website=worldfootball.net|publisher=World Football|access-date=4 March 2020}} On 28 April 2020, Prime Minister [[Édouard Philippe]] announced all sporting events in France, including those behind closed doors, would be banned until September.{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52460468|title=Ligue 1 & 2: France's top two divisions will not resume this season|date=28 April 2020|website=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|access-date=28 April 2020}} The FFF were considering whether the final of the Coupe de France could be rescheduled for when events are allowed to restart.{{cite web|url=https://www.fff.fr/actualites/190468-communique-de-la-fff-5?themePath=la-fff/|title=Communique de la FFF|website=FFF.fr|publisher=[[French Football Federation]]|language=fr|date=28 April 2020|access-date=13 January 2022|archive-date=6 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106112314/https://www.fff.fr/actualites/190468-communique-de-la-fff-5?themePath=la-fff%2F|url-status=dead}} On 26 June, the FFF announced that the final was rescheduled to 24 July. Paris Saint-Germain won the final 1–0 for their 13th Coupe de France title.{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-france-psg-ste-report/psg-beat-10-man-st-etienne-to-win-french-cup-but-mbappe-injured-idUSKCN24P2OJ|title=PSG beat 10-man St Etienne to win French Cup but Mbappe injured|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=25 July 2020|access-date=25 July 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53532177|title=Paris Saint-Germain 1–0 Saint-Étienne|website=BBC Sport|date=24 July 2020|access-date=24 July 2020}} ==Background== Paris Saint-Germain were the runners-up of last year's edition, having lost the [[2019 Coupe de France final|2019 final]] to [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] after a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] following a 2–2 draw in [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]].{{cite news|date=27 April 2019|title=Rennes stun PSG to win French Cup on penalties|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-france-ren-psg-report-idUKKCN1S30MH|publisher=[[Reuters]]|access-date=4 March 2020}}{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48071397|title=Rennes 2 PSG 2 (6-5 on penalties)|date=29 April 2019|website=BBC Sport|access-date=4 March 2020}} Saint-Étienne reached the final this year, having lost at the [[2018–19 Coupe de France#Round of 32|round of 32]] of last year's edition to [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]].{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/01/23/france/coupe-de-france/association-sportive-de-saint-etienne-loire/dijon-football-cote-dor/2957995/|title=Saint-Étienne vs. Dijon - 23 January 2019|website=soccerway.com|publisher=Soccerway|date=23 January 2019|access-date=5 March 2020}} This was the first time they reached the final since [[1982 Coupe de France final|1982]], a game they lost to Paris Saint-Germain as well.{{cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/20200306-saint-etienne-seal-comeback-win-to-reach-first-french-cup-final-since-1982|title=Saint-Etienne seal comeback win
